task: W2-92 (DAEO-n0wb) run 3, batch 9. Build DEC-1019 = P-W2-92-5 (a): when the record graph cannot be read, cite no record file, account for each one in `dropped`, and give the reason in the closure facet.
status: DONE. The change is committed and W2-92's acceptance passes on all 7 lines. W1-21's acceptance could not be run here (`gov accept DAEO-5x4l` refuses with ACCEPT_NO_MAP), so the lead needs to run it.
work_completed: I changed `src/gov/retrieval/retrieve.py` and added builder tests (TDD: red first, for the right reason, then green). When the record graph cannot be read, two kinds of file are now left out of the evidence. The first is any file whose front matter declares an `id`, read the way the store's loader reads a record (`loader._frontmatter`). The second is the register the path map names, found through `loader.PATH_MAP_REL` and `loader.REGISTER_KEY` with no new literal. Each one goes into `dropped` with the reason `NO_RECORD_GRAPH` and the front-matter id (the register uses its path). The closure facet's `unread` reason now ends with "record files are left out, as their currency cannot be judged without the record graph". Plain documents and code spans are still cited, and `stopping_reason` stays FACET_UNAVAILABLE. When the graph is present, neither new helper is ever called.
files_changed: src/gov/retrieval/retrieve.py (+32 −1: two helpers, `_declares_record` and `_named_register`, plus the `NO_RECORD_GRAPH` constant and the loader import, the extended `unread` text, the register named without the graph, and a 6-line block in the evidence loop); tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_92_record_files.py (new, 126 lines)
evidence: Commit e95eb4ad12ca "W2-92: no record file is cited without a record graph", trailers `Task: DAEO-n0wb`, `Role: engineer`, `Implements: DEC-423, DEC-957, DEC-424, CAP-12, CAP-13, CAP-18`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`. DEC-1019 is not in this worktree's register, so DEC-1019 and DEC-1006 are named in the commit body instead. No pre-commit hook was present (only `*.sample`). `git status` is clean after the commit. DEC-732: `python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` gives `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-92/src/gov/__init__.py`. To show nothing changes with the graph present, I dumped the bundles for 8 query and id cases on the new fixture at ac960862cfe7 before the edit, and again after it. With the temp root normalised the two files are byte-identical ("IDENTICAL").
tests: (1) The brief's command (test_w2_92_routes.py, tests/unit/retrieve, tests/unit/retrieval, tests/unit/closure, tests/unit/close/test_context.py) gives 162 passed, 1 skipped. The skip is `test_lexical.py:54`, which cannot import `govbridge` and was already skipped before. The new file (3 cases) is inside tests/unit/retrieval and passes. (2) `gov accept DAEO-n0wb --json` passes every line: success-1 9/0, success-2 7/0, success-3 6/0, success-4 9/0, failure-1 9/0, failure-2 6/0, failure-3 6/0 (passed/failed, 0 skipped on each). Unmapped 0/0/0. Totals 30 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. (3) `gov accept DAEO-5x4l --json` exits 1 with `ACCEPT_NO_MAP`: "ticket DAEO-5x4l: the README of tests/acceptance/W1-21/ maps no KPI line". No lines or counts were produced, so `test_without_a_record_graph_no_superseded_record_is_cited_as_current` has not been run by me.
discoveries: W1-21's acceptance folder has no README map that `gov accept` can read, so `gov accept` cannot run that ticket in this worktree. `gov retrieve` answered nothing useful here: lexical and semantic are both "stale", so it gave FACET_UNAVAILABLE with no evidence. The register path is only known from the graph (`authority.register_path(known)`), so without the graph it has to be read from the path map, which is what the new `_named_register` does.
risks: The product change is +32 −1 lines, above the brief's 15 to 25, because of the two small helpers and their docstrings. It fails closed: any chunked file whose front matter carries an `id` is left out, not only `.md` files. Without the graph, a non-Markdown file with such front matter is also withheld. If the path map cannot be read, no register is named and the register file would still be cited, but in that case the loader names no register either. My builder test plants the same four cases as W1-21's scenario (a SUPERSEDED record, an ACCEPTED record superseded by another, a dangling `superseded_by`, and the register). It does not prove the W1-21 case passes, because that has not been run.
lessons: `gov accept` for closed W1 tickets can fail on a missing README map. A graph-present bundle dumped before and after an edit is a cheap, strong way to prove "item for item unchanged". The scratch script is `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-92/eng9/dump.py`.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: The W1-21 acceptance case `test_without_a_record_graph_no_superseded_record_is_cited_as_current` still has to be run. `gov accept DAEO-5x4l` refuses with ACCEPT_NO_MAP, and as the brief says I did not look for another way to run it.
recommended_next_action: The lead runs W1-21's acceptance case in their slot against e95eb4ad12ca and confirms it passes.
